---

Seamless Auth is not a single package. It is a small ecosystem of projects that work together to
deliver passwordless authentication, self-hosted infrastructure, and operator tooling.

This page is the fastest way to understand what each repository is for and where to start.

---

## Mental Model

```txt
seamless-cli
  -> scaffolds and checks your local stack

seamless-auth-api
  -> runs the auth engine

@seamless-auth/express, @seamless-auth/fastify, @seamless-auth/nextjs, or @seamless-auth/core
(or seamless-auth for Python, seamless-auth-go for Go, seamless-auth for Rust)
  -> connects your backend to the auth engine

@seamless-auth/react, @seamless-auth/angular, @seamless-auth/vue, @seamless-auth/svelte, or
@seamless-auth/react-native
  -> connects your web or mobile frontend to the auth flow

seamless-auth-admin-dashboard
  -> gives operators a UI for users, organizations, sessions, events, security, and config
```

---

## The Main Pieces

| Project                         | What it is                                      | Use it when                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seamless-cli`                  | CLI for scaffolding and checking a local stack  | You want a working project (React or Next.js web, Express or Fastify API, optional Expo app) with auth wired  |
| `seamless-auth-api`             | Self-hostable auth server                       | You need the passwordless auth engine itself                                                                  |
| `@seamless-auth/core`           | Framework-agnostic server auth primitives       | You are building your own backend adapter                                                                     |
| `@seamless-auth/express`        | Official Express adapter                        | Your backend is Express (the most mature adapter path)                                                        |
| `@seamless-auth/fastify`        | Official Fastify adapter                        | Your backend is Fastify ([Server SDKs](/build/server-sdks#current-official-coverage))                         |
| `@seamless-auth/nextjs`         | Official Next.js App Router adapter             | Your Next.js app is its own backend ([Next.js](/build/nextjs))                                                |
| `seamless-auth` (PyPI)          | Official Python adapter                         | Your backend is FastAPI or Django ([Python](/build/python-adapter))                                           |
| `seamless-auth-go`              | Official Go adapter                             | Your backend is Go `net/http`, chi, Echo, or Gin ([Go](/build/go-adapter))                                    |
| `seamless-auth` (crates.io)     | Official Rust adapter                           | Your backend is Axum ([Rust](/build/rust-adapter))                                                            |
| `@seamless-auth/react`          | React SDK and built-in auth screens             | Your frontend is React and you want a ready-to-use auth integration                                           |
| `@seamless-auth/angular`        | Angular service, guards, and built-in screens   | Your frontend is Angular 20, 21, or 22 ([Angular SDK](/build/angular-sdk))                                    |
| `@seamless-auth/vue` | Vue plugin, composable, guards, and built-in screens | Your frontend is Vue 3.5 or later ([Vue SDK](/build/vue-sdk)) |
| `@seamless-auth/svelte` | Svelte session, SvelteKit guards, and built-in screens | Your frontend is Svelte 5 or SvelteKit ([Svelte SDK](/build/svelte-sdk)) |
| `@seamless-auth/react-native`   | React Native SDK: provider, hooks, native ports | Your frontend is an Expo or React Native app ([React Native SDK](/build/react-native-sdk))                    |
| `@seamless-auth/client`         | The framework-free client and sign-in flows the SDKs share | You are building a binding for another framework ([React SDK](/build/react-sdk#platform-ports-and-transport)) |
| `seamless-auth-admin-dashboard` | Operator dashboard app                          | You want a UI for admins and support teams                                                                    |
| `@seamless-auth/types`          | Shared request/response and domain types        | You want consistent types across apps and tooling                                                             |

---

## How The Pieces Fit

### 1. The Auth Server Is The Core

`seamless-auth-api` owns the authentication domain:

- registration
- login
- OTP flows
- WebAuthn / passkeys
- magic links
- OAuth
- TOTP / MFA
- sessions
- organizations
- JWKS
- system configuration
- admin and internal metrics endpoints

Everything else either talks to it directly or sits on top of it.

---

### 2. Server SDKs Protect Your API

Your application backend normally sits between the browser and the auth server.

That backend layer:

- owns the security boundary for your app
- validates cookies
- enforces authorization
- talks to the auth server using service-to-service credentials

If you use Express, start with `@seamless-auth/express`; Fastify, `@seamless-auth/fastify`; a
Next.js App Router application, `@seamless-auth/nextjs`. For FastAPI or Django, Go, or Axum, use the
[Python](/build/python-adapter), [Go](/build/go-adapter), or [Rust](/build/rust-adapter) adapter. If
you need a different Node.js runtime, start with `@seamless-auth/core`.

---

### 3. Frontend SDKs Drive The User Flow

`@seamless-auth/react` wraps your app with auth state and ships built-in auth routes for:

- login
- passkey login
- email / phone OTP verification
- magic link verification
- OAuth login helpers
- organization helpers
- step-up helpers
- WebAuthn PRF helpers
- passkey registration

The SDK gives you auth state and flow helpers, but your app still owns routing, authorization, and
product-specific UI decisions.

`@seamless-auth/angular` gives an Angular application the same state and flows as an injectable
service with signals and observables, functional route guards, and optional standalone screens that
match the React ones. See [Angular SDK](/build/angular-sdk).

`@seamless-auth/vue` does the same for Vue: a plugin and a `useSeamlessAuth()` composable returning
read-only refs, `vue-router` guards, and the same screens as named routes. See
[Vue SDK](/build/vue-sdk).

`@seamless-auth/svelte` gives a Svelte 5 application a session whose properties are runes,
SvelteKit `load` guards, and the same screens as components you mount at your routes. See
[Svelte SDK](/build/svelte-sdk).

`@seamless-auth/react-native` gives an Expo or React Native app the same state and headless client
over bearer transport, with native passkeys and the platform keystore behind ports. It ships no
screens. See [React Native SDK](/build/react-native-sdk).

---

### 4. The Admin Dashboard Is A Separate App

The admin dashboard is not built into the auth server. It is its own frontend application that
talks to the auth API.

That separation matters because:

- you can deploy the auth server without the dashboard
- you can customize the dashboard independently
- operator workflows stay separate from your end-user app

---

### 5. The CLI Connects Everything

`seamless-cli` is the fastest way to get a working stack. It scaffolds a web app (React or a
full-stack Next.js app), an API (Express or Fastify) unless the web template serves `/auth` itself,
an optional Expo mobile app, the auth server in Docker or local mode, and an optional admin console.

It also includes `check`, `verify`, and admin commands against a running instance. The first admin
is the account registered with the owner email `init` asks for. The current `../seamless-cli` source
does not ship `deploy`, `destroy`, or contributor workspace commands.

It is the easiest starting point if you want to learn the ecosystem through a working project
rather than by assembling every piece manually.

---

## Compatibility Matrix

Versions and declared ranges of the latest release of each package as of **2026-10-12**: the npm
`latest` tag for npm packages, and the latest GitHub Release for `seamless-auth-api` and
`seamless-auth-admin-dashboard`. Ranges are read from the released `package.json`. Every package
and the auth API require Node.js 22 or later (`engines.node` is `>=22`), except the messaging
packages, which require Node.js 18 or later.

| Package                           | Latest release | Declares on other Seamless packages                                                  | Other peer ranges                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seamless-auth-api`               | 0.18.0         | `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0, `@seamless-auth/messaging`, `-aws`, `-twilio` ^0.2.0 | None                                                                          |
| `@seamless-auth/core`             | 0.20.0         | `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0                                                       | None                                                                          |
| `@seamless-auth/express`          | 0.20.0         | `@seamless-auth/core` ^0.20.0                                                        | `express` >=5.0.0                                                             |
| `@seamless-auth/fastify`          | 0.11.1         | `@seamless-auth/core` ^0.20.0                                                        | `fastify` >=5.0.0                                                             |
| `@seamless-auth/nextjs`           | 0.4.0          | `@seamless-auth/core` ^0.20.0, `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0                        | None                                                                          |
| `@seamless-auth/client`           | 0.5.0          | `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0                                                       | None                                                                          |
| `@seamless-auth/react`            | 0.16.0         | `@seamless-auth/client` ^0.5.0, `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0                       | `react` and `react-dom` 18 or 19, optional `react-router-dom` 6.4+ or 7.15.1+ |
| `@seamless-auth/angular`          | 0.2.0          | `@seamless-auth/client` ^0.5.0                                                       | `@angular/core`, `common`, `router` 20, 21, or 22, and `rxjs` 7               |
| `@seamless-auth/vue` | 0.1.0 | `@seamless-auth/client` ^0.5.0 | `vue` 3.5+, optional `vue-router` 4.4+ or 5 |
| `@seamless-auth/svelte` | 0.1.0 | `@seamless-auth/client` ^0.5.0 | `svelte` 5, optional `@sveltejs/kit` 2.26+ or 3 |
| `@seamless-auth/react-native`     | 0.3.0          | `@seamless-auth/client` ^0.5.0, `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0                       | `react` 18 or 19                                                              |
| `@seamless-auth/types`            | 0.28.0         | None                                                                                 | None                                                                          |
| `@seamless-auth/messaging`        | 0.2.0          | None                                                                                 | None                                                                          |
| `@seamless-auth/messaging-aws`    | 0.2.0          | `@seamless-auth/messaging` ^0.2.0                                                    | None                                                                          |
| `@seamless-auth/messaging-twilio` | 0.2.0          | `@seamless-auth/messaging` ^0.2.0                                                    | None                                                                          |
| `seamless-cli`                    | 0.23.0         | `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0                                                       | None                                                                          |
| `seamless-auth-admin-dashboard`   | 0.9.1          | `@seamless-auth/react` ^0.15.1, `@seamless-auth/types` ^0.28.0                       | None                                                                          |

How to read it:

- Everything is still 0.x, and a caret range on a 0.x version pins the minor: `^0.19.0` accepts
  0.19.x but not 0.20.0. A package moves to a new minor of a dependency only when its own range is
  bumped and released.
- `@seamless-auth/express`, `fastify`, and `nextjs` declare `@seamless-auth/core` as
  `workspace:^`, which pnpm rewrites at publish to a caret on the core version in the same release
  (`^0.20.0` today).
- Every package that depends on `@seamless-auth/types` declares ^0.28.0, so an app that installs
  any mix of the SDKs and adapters resolves a single copy of it.
- The messaging packages are used by `seamless-auth-api` to deliver email and SMS. Your application
  does not install them.
- The auth API exposes an HTTP contract, not a package range. No package declares a range on
  `seamless-auth-api`, so pair the API and the server SDK from the same release window.

### Python, Go, And Rust Adapters

These are not npm packages, so they sit outside the table above and `npm run check:matrix`. Each
declares no range on another Seamless package; it reads the auth API's adapter manifest at runtime
instead.

| Adapter                              | Latest release | Registry                                     | Needs                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `seamless-auth` (Python)             | 0.2.0          | PyPI                                         | Python 3.11+, FastAPI 0.115+ or Django 5.2+, auth API v0.18.0+ |
| `github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-go` | v0.2.0     | Go module proxy (tag `v0.2.0`)               | Go 1.22+, auth API v0.18.0+                         |
| `seamless-auth` (Rust)               | 0.2.0          | crates.io                                    | Rust 1.88+, Axum 0.8, auth API v0.18.0+             |

### What The CLI Scaffolds

`seamless-cli` 0.23.0 does not install the newest of everything. It pins the images and the
template tag it scaffolds, so a given CLI version always produces the same project:

| What `seamless init` uses | Pinned to                                                      | Where it is set                                         |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Auth API image            | `ghcr.io/fells-code/seamless-auth-api:v0.18.0`                 | `seamless-cli` `src/core/images.ts`                     |
| Admin dashboard image     | `ghcr.io/fells-code/seamless-auth-admin-dashboard:v0.9.1`      | `seamless-cli` `src/core/images.ts`                     |
| Starter templates         | `fells-code/seamless-templates` at `v0.19.0`                   | `seamless-cli` `src/core/images.ts`                     |
| Express API template      | `@seamless-auth/express` ^0.19.1                               | `templates/api/express/package.json`                    |
| Fastify API template      | `@seamless-auth/fastify` ^0.10.1                               | `templates/api/fastify/package.json`                    |
| Next.js template          | `@seamless-auth/nextjs` ^0.3.1, `@seamless-auth/react` ^0.15.2 | `templates/fullstack/nextjs/package.json`               |
| React web templates       | `@seamless-auth/react` ^0.15.2                                 | `templates/web/react-vite`, `templates/web/react-oauth` |
| Angular, Vue, Svelte web templates | `@seamless-auth/angular` ^0.2.0, `@seamless-auth/vue` ^0.1.0, `@seamless-auth/svelte` ^0.1.0 | `templates/web/angular`, `templates/web/vue`, `templates/web/svelte` |
| Gin, Axum, FastAPI API templates | `seamless-auth-go` v0.2.0, `seamless-auth` crate 0.2, `seamless-auth[fastapi]` `>=0.2,<0.3` | `templates/api/gin/go.mod`, `templates/api/axum/Cargo.toml`, `templates/api/fastapi/pyproject.toml` |
| Expo template             | `@seamless-auth/react-native` ^0.2.2                           | `templates/mobile/expo/package.json`                    |
| Gin API template          | `github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-go` v0.2.0                | `templates/api/gin/go.mod`                              |
| Axum API template         | `seamless-auth` 0.2                                            | `templates/api/axum/Cargo.toml`                         |
| FastAPI API template      | `seamless-auth[fastapi]>=0.2,<0.3`                           | `templates/api/fastapi/pyproject.toml`                  |

Template paths are inside `fells-code/seamless-templates` at `v0.19.0`. A scaffolded project can
move to newer SDKs by bumping the ranges in its own `package.json`.

### Keeping This Matrix Current

Update this section in the same change that documents a release:

1. For each package published, set its version from its `package.json` on `main` and update every
   range that points at it (`dependencies` and `peerDependencies`).
2. When `seamless-cli` changes `SEAMLESS_AUTH_API_VERSION`, `SEAMLESS_AUTH_ADMIN_DASHBOARD_VERSION`,
   or `SEAMLESS_TEMPLATES_REF` in `src/core/images.ts`, update the scaffold table and re-read the
   template ranges at the new tag.
3. Change the date at the top of the section, then run `npm run check:matrix`.

`npm run check:matrix` (`scripts/check-compat-matrix.mjs`) reads the table above and compares each
"Latest release" with what is actually released: `npm view <package> version` for the npm packages, and
the latest GitHub release tag for `seamless-auth-api` and `seamless-auth-admin-dashboard`, which are
not published to npm. It prints `ok` or `drift` per row and exits 1 on any drift or on an npm
package it cannot look up. A GitHub row it cannot read (for example over the unauthenticated rate
limit) is skipped with a note. It needs the network, so it is not part of `npm run lint`. The
`check-compat-matrix` workflow runs it every Monday and on demand (`workflow_dispatch`), so a failed
run means a release has outpaced this table.

## Choose Your Starting Point

### I want a working stack quickly

Start with [Getting Started](/start/quickstart) and [CLI Overview](/operate/cli).

---

### I want to self-host the auth engine

Read [Auth API](/build/auth-api).

---

### I need to integrate my backend

Read [Server SDKs](/build/server-sdks) and [How To Secure Routes](/build/secure-routes).

---

### I need to integrate my React app

Read [React SDK](/build/react-sdk) and
[How To Build Your Own Auth UI](/build/custom-auth-ui).

---

### I need to integrate a mobile app

Read [React Native SDK](/build/react-native-sdk) and [Mobile Passkeys](/build/mobile-passkeys).
`seamless init --mobile=expo` scaffolds an Expo app next to the web and API projects.

---

### I need OAuth, teams, or MFA

Read [How To Add OAuth Login](/build/oauth-login),
[How To Use Organizations And Memberships](/build/organizations-memberships), and
[How To Use TOTP And Step-Up](/build/totp-step-up).

---

### I need an operator UI

Read [Admin Dashboard](/build/admin-dashboard).

---

## What This Docs Site Is Becoming

The docs are being reshaped around this ecosystem model:

- `Start` for guided onboarding
- `Build` for package and integration docs
- `Understand` for concepts and system behavior
- `Operate` for CLI and runtime workflows
- `Reference` for exact routes, env vars, and technical contracts

If a page makes a claim about a package or command, it should line up with the source repository for
that package or command.
